newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ARSENAL RAISE CHAMPIONSHIP HOPES WITH FOREIGN LEGION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARSENAL RAISE CHAMPIONSHIP HOPES WITH FOREIGN LEGION.

text.p: Juergen Klinsman, Eric Cantona and Juninho have all been and gone and left their mark on English soccer, but this season a new band of imports from just across the Channel are set to take the premier league by storm.
What is more, the majority of them all seem to be headed for Arsenal.

In a ground-breaking move, Arsenal's French manager Arsene Wenger, has signed five top class French players along with Dutch international Marc Overmars and a handful of others, to boost the north London club's chances of winning the league for the 11th time in its history and for the first time since 1991.
When the new season kicks-off on August 9 the Gunners are very likely to field six or seven foreign players in their first choice side -- a number unprecedented in the English League.
There is still much debate among the red half of North London whether the club are moving in the right direction. But if they win the league or FA Cup this season, the arguments will end.

Arsenal have never been without top class players but in the wake of the Bosman ruling, and in keeping with most of Europe's other major outfits, it has had an increasing number of overseas players arriving on its doorstep. Last season

Dutch and French internationals Dennis Bergkamp and Patrick Vieira brought a continental flavour to the side and helped Wenger, who moved to Arsenal nearly a year ago, eradicate the "boring boring" label it has had for generations. That tag
was acquired for the team's reliance on a solid defence. But Arsenal showed last season they can attack and entertain with the best. Wenger's fresh approach has been welcomed by the
players. "We needed a big squad with players who can pass
the ball. To play with possession suits us better," said Bergkamp. "You need players who, in one movement or with one touch, can change the game."
Wenger is an unlikely football manager. An economics graduate who speaks six languages, his injection of French flair has revolutionised Arsenal -- a club traditionally renowned for its conservatism.

Even so many were sceptical of his ability when he arrived but Wenger quickly won them over introducing new training techniques, including more ball work and shadow playing, to mould the team. "It's a calculated gamble putting so many
different, new elements together," he said. "Of course it will take time for foreign players to integrate into English football."
The new players would take their lead from the club's more experienced campaigners, he said. "Players like Tony Adams are winners. It's up to the new players to show they have the right spirit."
The influx of foreign players has coincided with Wenger's decision to sell England international Paul Merson -- at Arsenal since he was 14 -- a poignant symbol of the club's break with the past.
The Gunners -- who finished third last season -- now have a squad of 34 players, many of them internationals. For 24-year-old Overmars, that will only serve to produce better football.
"It's only good. The best 11 players will play, there is a lot of competition," he said.
It is in the running and passing skills of players such as Overmars that Wenger has invested Arsenal's future. And the squad are confident the strategy will reap rewards.

"I think with the players we have signed, the championship is well within our grasp," said 21-year-old French midfielder Patrick Vieira, who joined Arsenal last season. "The character of the players involved is exactly what the club's been looking for."
"We are here to win," added defender Emmanuel Petit who, with fellow Frenchman Gilles Grimandi, is looking to repeat the success he had with French championship winners Monaco last season.
Wenger, who guided Monaco to the French title in 1988, also appears to have quickly won over his established players with his new signings.
"I will have to help them," said Wright, now 33 and who should break the club's all-time scoring record during the coming season.
He believes the new arrivals have rejuvenated him and feels the players can push each other to new heights.
"I'm excited for the new players. I want them to do well because in the end I will do well," he said. And he was happy with Wenger's management style.
"He virtually said to me that 'your place will be there for as long as you're fit to claim it' and you can't be fairer than that."

Questions might be asked about whether Wenger can successfully blend together his band of internationals for Arsenal to win the title. After all, Middlesbrough built a team based on players whose names ended with vowels and who ended up being relegated last season.
But there is no mistaking the excitement and air of anticipation about Highbury as they prepare for the new season -- there is an appetite for success.
"You have to earn a championship medal and I feel I'm in a position to get one," said Wright.
Bergkamp agreed: "I think it's time now to win some prizes." REUTER
